reasons: Both answers steel-man the 15-minute revocation gap, give an honest verdict and propose sid/token_version fixes without migration. B states outright that the Postgres refresh-token table already makes the scheme stateful, which is rubric item 2. A only touches this indirectly through the hot-path framing and the 'Postgres is also a SPOF' retort. B also correctly notes that XSS can call /refresh same-origin, and it gives a clearer mitigation table.

A: Says the IETF browser-based apps draft is primarily aimed against tokens in localStorage, which understates its concern that in-memory tokens can also be obtained via XSS (e.g. by calling the refresh endpoint)
